segments.title: Chương 33: Dì Tao rất vui
segments.content:
Tao Xue wasn't interested in playing games, so she squatted under a camphor tree, poking at ants.

She picked up a twig and started toying with one of the ants.

When the ant crawled a few centimeters, she would block its path with the twig, startling the ant into changing its direction.

What a little devil, so naughty!

Xie Yang, however, perked up his ears, eavesdropping on Chen Guiliang's phone call.

The guy's great ambition at this moment wasn't to pass the civil service exam and become an official, but to become the richest man in China by making games.

Chen Guiliang continued, "I've thought about it carefully again these past few days. Miracles itself has a weapon upgrade system. We can start from there; we don't need to add any new features. The jewelry that drops from instance dungeons with a guarantee can be used by players to upgrade their weapons. This way, we can deal with the excess super-powered jewelry that rich players get from repeatedly running dungeons, and it will increase their motivation to keep running them."

Tao Chenggang praised, "Not bad, not bad at all!"

Unfortunately, the official Miracles server had not yet introduced features like socketing equipment or adding gems. This kind of gameplay required adding new features, which was a bit difficult technically.

Chen Guiliang continued, "To increase game immersion, we can add a dialogue for the player with the old soldier who teleports them to the instance dungeon to flesh out the world-building. We'll say that during the great war between good and evil, a mysterious void power invaded. Those dungeons are all projections of the real world within the abyssal rifts. The super-powered equipment that's hard to name can all have 'Abyss' or 'Void' added as a prefix."

Tao Chenggang laughed loudly. "I've never seen someone making a private server who also has to write a story for it."

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm a bit of a perfectionist."

"Fine, we'll do as you say. It's just adding a piece of dialogue, after all," Tao Chenggang said.

Chen Guiliang reminded him again, "Remember, our main promotional point is: we don't sell equipment, everything is earned through playing. You and Brother Yang should write an article, recounting your experiences playing Miracles over the years. Write about your happiness, sadness, friendships, and so on. It's best if you can include all the major events in Miracles' history."

"You mean that promotional article?" Tao Chenggang asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Yes, the more sentimental, the better. When you're done, send it to my email. I'll polish it up and then post it on the forums."

The two continued their conversation for more than ten minutes before finally ending the call.

Chen Guiliang also sent his email address over via text message.

This was an email he had applied for at his cousin's house earlier. He had long forgotten his high school email from his previous life.

Just as Chen Guiliang put his "Xiao Lingtong" phone back into his pocket, Xie Yang asked impatiently, "What's going on? Are you making a private server with someone?"

"You know about private servers too?" Chen Guiliang retorted.

Xie Yang said, "I'm a veteran Miracles player, how could I not know about private servers? Every internet cafe has a Miracles private server, but they're really boring to play. Take Huayu Internet Cafe for example, the highest-level map is only Zuma Temple."

This so-called "Huayu Internet Cafe" was, of course, a knockoff and not a real chain brand.

Xie Yang often went to Huayu Internet Cafe. The computers there were the worst, so it was also the cheapest, with a membership price of only 1.5 yuan per hour.

The Miracles private server in Huayu Internet Cafe was built on a junk framework that the cafe manager downloaded for free, with the server set up right there in the cafe. Surprisingly, people actually played this kind of thing, and some even topped up to buy equipment, allowing the manager to earn some pocket money.

"How did you get into making a private server?" Xie Yang pressed.

Chen Guiliang explained simply, "I know a boss who runs an internet cafe, and I gave him some game ideas."

Xie Yang pushed further, "Does it make money?"

"It might make money," Chen Guiliang said evasively.

Xie Yang said excitedly, "Count me in. I don't want any money, I just want to be a part of it."

He felt that just by participating, he would be doing something big. Whether it made money or not didn't matter.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "I'll call you when it's online. I'll give you a few pieces of super-powered equipment, and you can be a shill in the game, guiding the rich players to top up. Or, you can help reply to posts on the forums to promote it."

Hearing this, Xie Yang became even more thrilled. "Don't worry, I know what to do!"

Chen Guiliang reminded him, "Don't go blabbing about this. Running a private server is illegal, after all. Don't spread it around in class or the dorm."

"I know, I won't tell anyone," Xie Yang said, patting his chest in guarantee.

Chen Guiliang was quite confident in him. Although Xie Yang was usually flighty, he was always reliable when it mattered.

Tao Xue finally stopped teasing the ants, tossed the twig aside and said, "Are you guys done talking?"

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Thank you, Auntie Tao, for making a special trip to bring me the Xiao Lingtong."

"It's not just that I brought it. I personally went to buy it this afternoon, and I even helped you sign up for a plan and top it up," Tao Xue once again emphasized her great deeds.

Chen Guiliang said with a grin, "You're the auntie, of course the elder has to work a bit harder."

Tao Xue was smug, continuing to take advantage. "Then from now on, you're not Senior Zhang Wei anymore. You're my little nephew… no, that's not right, you're my big nephew."

She was especially happy now. She had always been fooled by Chen Guiliang before, but now she had finally scored a point back.

A huge win!

Chen Guiliang called her "Auntie Tao" a few more times, charming her until she was completely giddy.

"Auntie Tao, wait here for a moment," Chen Guiliang said, quickly running back to the dorm.

When he reappeared, he had a book in his hand.

"For me?" Tao Xue asked, pleasantly surprised.

"It's only polite to return a favor," Chen Guiliang said. "It's Haizi's poetry, a genuine copy I bought from Xinhua Bookstore. It has my thoughts on the poems inside."

This literary girl was a bit too lively and cheerful.

Maybe reading more of Haizi's poetry could make her a little more melancholic.

What a dog. "Thank you, big nephew." Tao Xue's eyes curved into crescent moons as she smiled.

Chen Guiliang continued to dangle a carrot. "If I pass the preliminary round of the New Concept Writing Competition, I'll get to meet a lot of authors. I can get you a few autographs then."

Tao Xue was even happier. "Get me Yu Hua's autograph. Bring my copy of To Live when you go, have him sign it on the title page. It would be best if he could write a blessing."

"No problem," Chen Guiliang agreed instantly.

Tao Xue's mood became even better. She continued to chat idly with Chen Guiliang, occasionally exchanging a few words with Xie Yang.

Only when the evening self-study session was about to begin did she wave goodbye cheerfully, skipping off to the classroom with the book of Haizi's poetry.

Even after Tao Xue had left, Xie Yang was still brimming with excitement.

"Heh~~Ha!"

Xie Yang paced back and forth under the camphor tree, finally resorting to punching and kicking the tree trunk to release the irrepressible excitement in his heart.

"Let's go, time for evening self-study," Chen Guiliang reminded him.

Xie Yang caught up in a few steps and praised him sincerely, "Hero Chen, you're so fucking awesome! Seriously, I've wanted to make a game for a long time. I was planning to do it in college, but I never thought I'd get to participate in high school."

He had always been lost, not knowing what to do. Now, he finally had something to work on.

At the same time, more questions surfaced in his mind.

Why would Chen Guiliang, who never played online games, suddenly partner up with someone to make a private server? And how could he give them ideas?

Hero Chen was becoming more and more mysterious.

He had been mysterious before, too. Xie Yang had never been able to figure him out.

As they reached the academic building, Xie Yang said with high spirits, "Hero Chen, when we go to university later, we can choose the same city. During our college years, I'll follow you in starting a business, and we'll take the world by storm and do great things together!"

Chen Guiliang chuckled. "Damn, your choice of words is quite bold."

Evening self-study.

The form teacher, Liu Shuying, walked into the classroom.

"We had the parent-teacher conference last weekend. The teachers and parents exchanged opinions, and we all think the seating arrangement should be adjusted again."

"In other classes, seats are arranged according to grades. But our Class 11 is an experimental class, and everyone is a good student. I didn't think it was necessary to embarrass anyone, so most of the time, I assigned seats randomly, with minor adjustments based on height."

"Now that it's the third year of high school, since some students have no sense of shame or ambition, we will be rearranging the seats according to the mid-term exam results."

"From now until the Gaokao, we will change seats after every mid-term, final, and mock exam!"

"Wu Meng, you sit in the middle of the first row."

Wu Meng was next year's top liberal arts scorer for the entire city. She had ranked first in the whole school in this mid-term exam.

Most of the students in the class cast envious glances at Wu Meng.

Except for the underachievers, who didn't want to sit in the front.

Liu Shuying said again, "Student Bian Guanyue, although you didn't take the mid-term exam, you've been studying hard and diligently during this time. Bian Guanyue, you'll be Wu Meng's deskmate."

As soon as these words were spoken, all the students in the class looked toward the back row.

Something was fishy!

Bian Guanyue immediately refused, "Teacher Liu, I don't think this is fair. I didn't take the mid-term exam."

"This is my arrangement," Liu Shuying said. "If your final exam results are not good, I will move you back to the rear again."

Bian Guanyue was holding back her anger. She guessed her father had pulled some strings.

Her father was always interfering with her studies and her life!

Liu Shuying stood silently, waiting for Bian Guanyue to move her seat. The other students were waiting too.

Bian Guanyue could only compromise. She couldn't disrupt and affect the entire class because of a conflict between her father and her.

Seeing Bian Guanyue walk towards the front row carrying her schoolbag and holding her books and exam papers, Li Jun gloatingly and sneakily gave Chen Guiliang the middle finger.

Chen Guiliang acted as if he didn't see it.

Once Bian Guanyue was seated at the desk in front of the teacher's podium, Liu Shuying finally breathed a sigh of relief. She had to complete the task assigned by the head of academic affairs.

"Li Rui, you sit at the desk to Wu Meng's left." Liu Shuying held the mid-term grade sheet and continued to call out students' names.

Chen Guiliang, who had only done the multiple-choice questions in math and failed English and liberal arts comprehensive, was surprisingly moved to the second to last row this time.

Because two other students had, without a sound, scored even worse than him.

"Hero Chen, hello there." His new deskmate, Qin Shanshan, walked over with her books and exam papers, smiling.

"Hello."

Chen Guiliang didn't have a deep impression of Qin Shanshan. He only knew her parents both worked for the tobacco company, and in his past life, she had chosen to repeat the year after failing to get into a second-tier university.

She also liked to wear makeup and could be considered pretty.

The form teacher's sudden seat change had somewhat affected Chen Guiliang's plans.

But it didn't matter.

Evening self-study at No. 2 High School lasted for a full 2 hours and 15 minutes. One hour per session, with a 15-minute break in between.

The form teacher, Liu Shuying, supervised for an hour before leaving.

Chen Guiliang took advantage of the break to run to the restroom, but he was actually trying to skip a session of evening self-study. Tao Chenggang had sent him a text message, saying that the promotional article had been sent to his email.

"You're going to skip class?" Xie Yang appeared stealthily.

Chen Guiliang jumped. "How do you walk so silently?"

Xie Yang said, "It's you who has a guilty conscience."

The two took a detour towards the school's back gate, afraid of running into the form teacher.

Arriving at the street of internet cafes, business here was booming. They went to two cafes in a row without finding any open seats. Most of the customers were students who had skipped evening self-study to surf the internet!

Of course, not all of them were from No. 2 High School.

Because next door was No. 7 High School, as well as its junior high division.

The three schools combined had a total student population of over ten thousand, so the street of internet cafes never had to worry about customers.

When it came to skipping class to go online, No. 7 High School was even more impressive. Hardly anyone stayed in the classrooms for evening self-study.

To put it this way, with Xie Yang's current poor grades, if he transferred to No. 7 High School, he could easily rank first in the entire school.

They finally found an internet cafe with empty seats. As soon as Chen Guiliang got on a computer, he opened his email. The title of the advertorial sent by Tao Chenggang was: What Games Can We Old Miracles Players Still Play Now?

Chen Guiliang read it carefully. His evaluation of the article was "detailed in content, but lacking in sentimentality."

He would have to polish it himself.

Soon, the title was changed by Chen Guiliang to: The Heartfelt Words of a Miracles Refugee: The Internet is So Big, But Where is My Home?

Xie Yang logged on but didn't play any games. He sat over to watch Chen Guiliang edit the article, and based on his own gaming experience, he occasionally offered some suggestions for changes.

It took half an hour to finish all the edits. Chen Guiliang chatted with Tao Chenggang on QQ, "Post this article first on 17173, which has the most traffic. Have the studio's hired posters get the thread hot, then repost it to 17577 and other private server forums in the form of a spontaneous repost by a netizen."

The terms "traffic" and "hired posters" were definitions given by Chen Guiliang. Tao Chenggang, Yang Yuhui, and Feng Tao had already gotten used to them.

Tao Chenggang received the email, read the article carefully, and immediately replied on QQ, "You're fucking brilliant! The content of the article is still the same, the people and events haven't changed, but just by changing the wording and sentence structure, it's become incredibly sentimental."

Xie Yang, sitting beside him, said, "Once this article is out, it's definitely going to be a hit on the gaming forums."

(Seeking guaranteed monthly votes.)
